findings.description: The opt-in reader checks `merged.get("headless")`, but the documented and tested user-facing key is `hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in`. In the actual `.loa.config.yaml.example` the setting is nested under `hounfour`, so a real config with `hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in: true` will still read as disabled unless the loader strips `hounfour` elsewhere. The new tests do not catch this because `_project()` writes a `.loa.config.yaml` whose top-level content starts with `hounfour`, yet the assertion expects `True`; if `load_project_config()` preserves the documented shape, this test should fail, indicating the implementation is reading the wrong path.
findings.failure_mode: Operators who explicitly opt in via the documented key cannot use the agy route: `complete()` raises `AgyOptInRequiredError`, `health_check()` stays false, and planners mark the voice as not planned despite valid configuration.
findings.suggested_fix: Read the nested path from the merged config, e.g. `hounfour = merged.get("hounfour") if isinstance(merged, dict) else None; headless = hounfour.get("headless") if isinstance(hounfour, dict) else None`, or use the same normalized accessor already used by the rest of the loader if one exists. Keep tests pinned to the real loader shape.

findings.cross_file_justification: The refusal is raised from complete() as a ConfigError subclass (INVALID_CONFIG, retryable=False). By this adapter's own documented classification (_raise_for_error comments: ConfigError = 'hard-abort (static misconfig)', ProviderUnavailableError = 'WALK the chain'), cheval's Python fallback-chain walker in cheval.py treats ConfigError as non-walkable. The FR-1 file list in the report touches four bash planners and Bridgebuilder but not cheval.py's chain resolution, so cheval's own chains still contain the gemini-headless hop.
findings.description: The spec (FR-1 / G-1) requires an opt-in-off agy hop to be recorded as 'not planned, never as a failed voice'. The bash planners achieve this by filtering the hop out of the chain before calling cheval (_adv_agy_filter_chain). cheval's own chain walk was not given the equivalent filter, and the gate raises a hard-abort ConfigError. For any direct cheval caller whose chain reaches the gemini-headless hop: (a) with the stock ordering (API hops first, agy terminal), an upstream walkable failure such as a 429 on gemini-api is masked by a terminal INVALID_CONFIG 'opt-in required' error; (b) with `hounfour.headless.mode: prefer-cli` (documented in the example config), the agy hop is tried first and the chain aborts before the gemini-api hop runs, so the Google voice is lost entirely on a host that merely has not opted in, instead of falling through to the API. Nothing in the diff or tests exercises a chain with the hop in a non-terminal position.
findings.failure_mode: A prefer-cli operator who upgrades without setting agy_opt_in: true loses the Google voice completely: every chain that routes through gemini-headless raises INVALID_CONFIG at the first hop and never reaches gemini-api. With stock ordering, the real upstream failure is hidden behind an opt-in message, misdirecting triage.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (1) have the chain resolver in cheval.py drop gemini-headless hops when agy_opt_in_enabled() is False (mirroring _adv_agy_filter_chain) and WARN once that the hop is not planned, so the hop is never dispatched and never recorded as a failure; or (2) if the hop must stay in the chain, make the refusal walkable (a ProviderUnavailableError subclass carrying failure_class='opt_in_required') so the chain advances to the API hop. Add a test with chain [gemini-headless, gemini-api] and opt-in off asserting gemini-api is dispatched.

findings.description: `root = project_root or _find_project_root()` runs outside the `try` that implements fail-closed. If root discovery raises (e.g. os.getcwd()/Path.cwd() FileNotFoundError when the process cwd has vanished, a condition this adapter already defends against via cwd_vanished, or a no-root-found error), the exception escapes agy_opt_in_enabled and complete()/health_check() surface a raw untyped exception instead of the AgyOptInRequiredError refusal.
findings.failure_mode: Callers expecting a typed ChevalError (chain walker, JSON error envelope) get an unclassified traceback from inside the gate, and health_check() raises instead of returning False.
findings.suggested_fix: Move root resolution inside the try block so any failure to locate or read config returns False, matching the docstring's 'a config that cannot be read reads as off'.

findings.description: When the opt-in is off, validate_config() appends the opt-in error but then continues to shutil.which() the binary and to emit "'agy' CLI not found on PATH. Install + OAuth-authenticate..." on a host without agy. The module docstring claims the gate runs 'before any binary discovery'; here discovery still happens, and a host that deliberately has not opted in is told to install agy. Any consumer of validate_config (e.g. a `cheval validate`/preflight path) will report the un-planned hop as a missing-binary misconfiguration, which is exactly the 'failed voice' reading FR-1 is meant to remove.
findings.failure_mode: Operators on hosts without agy see two errors for the gemini-headless provider, one of which instructs them to install and authenticate agy even though the route is intentionally disabled.
findings.suggested_fix: Return early after appending the opt-in error (or skip the PATH probe and the install instruction while the opt-in is off), and add an assertion in test_off_validate_config_names_the_key that shutil.which is not called and no 'not found on PATH' error is emitted.

findings.cross_file_justification: The class docstring states failure_class / context['failure_class'] is 'the machine-readable seam planners read'. Whether that seam reaches consumers depends on cheval.py's error-to-JSON serialization, which is outside the diff. The reviewer context's e2e evidence for the refusal shows only {"error": true, "code": "INVALID_CONFIG", "message": ...} with no failure_class or context field.
findings.description: self.context is assigned after super().__init__(), so if ChevalError's serializer builds the envelope from constructor args or does not include context, the machine-readable seam is never emitted and callers of the cheval CLI can only distinguish this refusal from any other INVALID_CONFIG by substring-matching the human message. The in-process test asserts only on the Python attribute, not on the serialized envelope.
findings.failure_mode: External planners that consume cheval's JSON (rather than re-reading the YAML with yq) cannot tell 'not planned' from a genuine misconfiguration and fall back to brittle message grepping.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass context through ChevalError.__init__ if it accepts it, and add a test that the CLI's JSON error envelope for this refusal carries failure_class: opt_in_required; or document that the seam is Python-only.

findings.description: The gate changes the default behaviour of every code path that constructs the gemini-headless adapter, but only three test modules received the autouse opt-in fixture, and the report states the adapters suite was run with a -k filter ('effort or ceiling or probe or catalog_floor or trust or agy or headless or opus55 or literal'), not in full. Any existing test outside that selection that dispatches or health-checks gemini-headless (chain/fallback tests, registry tests, cheval CLI tests, circuit-breaker tests) now reads the real project config from the test cwd and will receive AgyOptInRequiredError or health_check()==False.
findings.failure_mode: Red tests in CI outside the filtered selection, or worse, tests that silently pass because a mocked chain now skips a hop that used to be exercised.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the full .claude/adapters pytest suite once before merge; where unrelated suites touch gemini-headless, either add the same autouse fixture via a shared conftest or point them at a tmp project with agy_opt_in: true.

findings.description: The gate merges load_system_defaults(root) under the project config, so a framework-shipped defaults file (.claude/defaults, updated on framework upgrade rather than by the operator) can satisfy the opt-in. The example config and the module docstring describe the key as an operator decision in .loa.config.yaml only. Env overrides were deliberately excluded for the same reason; the defaults layer is a comparable non-operator channel for a flag whose purpose is to require a deliberate local choice about exposing the prompt on argv.
findings.failure_mode: A future defaults change (or a vendored defaults file in a template) flips every project to opted-in without any edit to the project's own config.
findings.suggested_fix: Read the key from load_project_config(root) only (optionally still inside the fail-closed try), and add a parametrized case asserting that agy_opt_in: true in the system defaults alone does not enable the route.

findings.description: The companion-chain filter treats a hop as agy-routed only when _adv_hop_canon yields the literal 'gemini-headless'. The sibling predicate added in the same change, flatline-orchestrator.sh:_tertiary_routes_to_agy, documents that cheval also dispatches any Google/gemini* model through agy when hounfour.headless.mode is 'cli-only' (LOA_HEADLESS_MODE winning, 'as cheval's'). The dissent filter, run-preflight.sh P3 (cli_for only matches the bare 'gemini-headless' id, so a gemini-* model in cli-only mode is counted usable on a Google credential) and loa-status.sh all ignore that path. The four readers the report calls 'yq twins' therefore disagree on which voices are gated.
findings.failure_mode: With hounfour.headless.mode: cli-only and the opt-in off (the default), a companion chain naming gemini-2.5-pro or google:gemini-* is planned, cheval refuses it with INVALID_CONFIG / opt_in_required, and the dissent records a failed companion (verdict DEGRADED) instead of planned: false, reason: opt_in_required. run-preflight P3 reports the same voice usable and passes a run that cannot dispatch it. This violates the FR-1 AC and G-1 ('no planned voice that cannot exist') in a supported configuration.
findings.suggested_fix: Define one routes-to-agy predicate with the flatline shape (literal gemini-headless hop, or gemini*/google:gemini* when the effective headless mode is cli-only) and use it in _adv_agy_filter_chain, in the run-preflight P3 loop (classify the voice as not planned), and in loa-status _provider_hop/_provider_hop_note. Add a bats case per planner with mode: cli-only and a gemini-2.5-pro voice asserting opt_in_required / not planned.

findings.description: Only the companion chain is passed through _adv_agy_filter_chain. The primary review's model / fallback_chain for flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit} can also name gemini-headless, and nothing in the diff gates or warns about it on the primary path.
findings.failure_mode: With the opt-in off, the primary attempts the agy hop and receives INVALID_CONFIG from cheval. If the primary fallback does not advance past INVALID_CONFIG the review fails outright; if it does advance, the drop happens silently with no 'not planned' WARN, unlike the companion path.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the primary chain through the same filter (logging the WARN with the stage key), or confirm that INVALID_CONFIG advances the primary fallback and add a test for a primary chain containing gemini-headless with the opt-in off.

findings.description: The change introduces two new values into emitted metadata: tertiary_model_status may now be 'disabled_by_opt_in' (Flatline result JSON) and companion_skip_reason may now be 'opt_in_required' (dissent envelope). The diff does not touch any schema or consumer of those fields.
findings.failure_mode: Any schema, Bridgebuilder parser, run-status display or dashboard that validates these fields against the previous closed sets (active|disabled; no_route|...) will reject the output or mis-bucket the run as a degraded voice, which is the exact outcome FR-1 is meant to avoid.
findings.suggested_fix: Grep .claude/data/schemas and the consumers for tertiary_model_status / companion_skip_reason enums, extend them with the new values, and add a test that the produced JSON validates against the schema.

findings.description: When every configured voice of a stage is a gated agy hop, the loop 'continue's past them, usable stays 0, and P3 is recorded FAIL with detail 'no usable voice ... no credential present and no CLI hop on PATH' and the generic fix hint to export a key or install a CLI hop. Only the appended 'not planned:' suffix mentions the opt-in.
findings.failure_mode: The operator is told to install agy or export GOOGLE_API_KEY; neither changes the outcome, because the voice is gated by hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in. The P3 fix text is wrong for this case.
findings.suggested_fix: Track per-stage whether all skipped voices were opt-in gated; when such a stage fails, set the detail to 'no planned voice for <stage>: agy route disabled by opt-in' and the fix to 'set hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in: true in .loa.config.yaml or name another voice in the stage's fallback_chain'.

findings.description: The first hunk is attributed to the production dispatcher .claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh, but its added lines and its pre-existing context lines are bats @test blocks that use $T, $CALLS, _run_main, BEHAVIOUR[...] and `return 1`. This is almost certainly tests/unit/adversarial-review-companion.bats mislabelled by the diff tooling, but the bundle cannot confirm it, and the dispatcher-side changes the report claims (_adv_agy_opted_in, _adv_agy_filter_chain, companion_skip_reason=opt_in_required) are then absent from what was reviewed.
findings.failure_mode: If the hunk really landed in the .sh file, bash reaches `@test ... {` after main returns, errors on `@test` and `local`, then executes the `for` loop body at top level: _cmp_agy_chain rewrites $CONFIG_FILE (the operator's live config) and _run_main review is invoked outside any test sandbox. If the path is a labelling artefact, the production gate code was not part of this review.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm with `git show --stat` that CMP-284..286 live in tests/unit/adversarial-review-companion.bats, and re-run the review with the actual .claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh hunks included.

findings.cross_file_justification: FTA-2 pins the planner decision in .claude/scripts/flatline-orchestrator.sh:_tertiary_routes_to_agy, which must agree with the dispatch-time gate in .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/agy_headless_adapter.py:complete for G-1 to hold.
findings.description: FTA-2 asserts that under hounfour.headless.mode prefer-api a Google tertiary (gemini-3.1-pro) is planned as `active`. The test neither sets nor clears GOOGLE_API_KEY/GEMINI_API_KEY, so the planner must be ignoring key presence. prefer-api semantics fall back to the CLI hop when no API key is resolvable, and the Google CLI hop is agy, which complete() now refuses with opt_in_required before any spawn.
findings.failure_mode: An operator with no Google key who relied on agy under the default mode (the pre-cycle-127 norm) gets a tertiary that is planned, dispatched, refused by the adapter, and recorded as a dropped voice / DEGRADED. That is exactly the 'planned voice that cannot exist' FR-1 and G-1 set out to remove, and the suite cannot see it because the gate is only asserted for cli-only and for the literal gemini-headless alias.
findings.suggested_fix: Have _tertiary_routes_to_agy (and the companion, preflight and Bridgebuilder twins) treat a Google voice as agy-routed under prefer-api when no Google key is resolvable, or map a dispatch-time opt_in_required failure to disabled_by_opt_in instead of a dropped voice. Add an FTA case: prefer-api, GOOGLE_API_KEY/GEMINI_API_KEY unset, tertiary gemini-3.1-pro → not planned; and its mirror with a key present → planned.

findings.description: The rewritten LSP-5 pins that once ceiling_calibration.calibrated_at is set, a PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT observation below the calibrated bound neither lowers the bound nor appears in the /loa line or --json (only `calibrated $eff ($m, calibrated $cal)` is asserted for all three runs). The committed calibration came from a single route (claude-bedrock global, tool outcome `partial`, I2-clamped to 936000) and applies to claude-opus-5-5 on every anthropic route.
findings.failure_mode: On a route whose real input limit is lower (a non-global Bedrock region, Vertex, or a direct-API tier without the 1M window), cheval keeps sizing requests to 936000, receives a verified context-limit rejection every time, and the previously self-healing path (uncalibrated: a verified observation becomes the bound) is disabled with no operator-visible signal in /loa.
findings.suggested_fix: Let a verified PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT (not the *_UNVERIFIED classes) lower a calibrated bound, or at minimum render it (`calibrated 936000; observed N below, reprobe suggested`) in both the text line and --json, and pin that in LSP-5 instead of asserting silence.

findings.description: LSP-5 now selects its assertions from the committed catalog (`if [[ -n "$cal" ]]`). Since the catalog carries calibrated_at for claude-opus-5-5, every `else` branch (the `probed` display, `observed N under the opt-in`, and `an observation below the probed bound becomes the bound`) is dead in CI. The literal-pinned assertions that did exercise those paths were removed, and the test title still promises them.
findings.failure_mode: A regression in the probed/observed rendering or in the observation-lowering logic for any uncalibrated anthropic model ships green.
findings.suggested_fix: Split into two tests. Drive the uncalibrated one against a fixture catalog via a bats-gated override (as LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE already does for the config) or against a second anthropic entry with no ceiling_calibration, so both branches run on every pass.

findings.cross_file_justification: Four independent yq readers of hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in (adversarial-review.sh, flatline-orchestrator.sh, run-preflight.sh, loa-status.sh) plus the Python predicate must agree; the report states they are copies rather than one shared helper.
findings.description: CMP-284, FTA-1 and PF-AGY all pin that the YAML string "true" is not the boolean and leaves the gate off. LSP-AGY only exercises absent and boolean true. `yq -r '.hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in'` prints `true` for both forms, so a reader that compares the raw string (rather than checking `tag == "!!bool"`) silently accepts the quoted value. Separately, no reader emits a diagnostic for a value that is present but not a boolean.
findings.failure_mode: /loa Providers could report `hop agy` (opted in) while cheval, Flatline, the dissent and preflight treat the same config as opted out, a misleading diagnostic for precisely the operator who mistyped the value. That operator otherwise sees only `opt-in (disabled)` with no hint their setting was ignored.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the "true" string case to LSP-AGY, add a conformance test that feeds the same three configs to all four bash readers and the Python predicate, and emit a one-line WARN naming the key when the value is present but not a YAML boolean.

findings.description: _cmp_agy_chain rewrites $CONFIG_FILE, but CMP-284's per-iteration save/restore copies $T/loa.config.yaml and tolerates a missing source (`cp ... 2>/dev/null || true`). The helper's `str.replace(..., 1)` never asserts that the `code_review:\n    enabled: true` anchor was found.
findings.failure_mode: If CONFIG_FILE ever points elsewhere, iterations stack a second companion_chain key and repeated top-level hounfour keys; because all three expected outcomes are 'off', the loop keeps passing for the wrong reason. If the fixture block changes shape, the chain is never inserted and the failure surfaces as an unrelated planned/reason mismatch.
findings.suggested_fix: Save and restore $CONFIG_FILE, drop `|| true`, and assert in the Python that exactly one replacement happened before writing.

findings.description: FTA-5 is the only test that runs run_phase1 through the new disabled_by_opt_in branch, and it never checks $status after `run --separate-stderr run_phase1 ...`. The assertions (four calls, the skip line, no 'Voice dropped') are all satisfied even if run_phase1 aborts after dispatch.
findings.failure_mode: A crash in the 2-model path after the skip is logged (for example a later step that still dereferences the tertiary's output file) ships with this test green.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `[ "$status" -eq 0 ]` after the run and assert the Phase 1 output artefact exists in $TEMP_DIR.

findings.description: readAgyGate swallows every failure of the yq read (binary missing, YAML parse error, timeout, non-JSON output) and returns {optIn: false, mode: ''}. Two consequences: (1) an operator who set hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in: true but has a broken or absent yq sees the google voice dropped with the pipeline's info line 'agy opt-in off', which is false and points them at the wrong fix; (2) the mode collapses to 'prefer-api', so under a cli-only config Bridgebuilder plans a google voice that cheval (reading the same file through its Python loader) will refuse with AgyOptInRequiredError, producing a failed voice and a blocked merge instead of the 'not planned' outcome FR-1 specifies. The read failure is never logged anywhere.
findings.failure_mode: Silent divergence between Bridgebuilder's gate and cheval's gate on hosts where yq is unavailable or the config is malformed; misleading operator log; G-1 ('no planned voice that cannot exist') violated in exactly the environment where diagnosis is hardest.
findings.suggested_fix: Return a third state (e.g. readError?: string) from readAgyGate and have executeMultiModelReview log it at warn level with the underlying error. Keep the fail-closed opt-in default, but do not report a read failure as 'opt-in off'. Optionally reuse the existing config loader in config.ts (which already shells to yq) so there is one read path.

findings.description: api_key_mode: 'strict' still only throws on keyStatus.missing. A voice removed by the agy gate is not in missing, so a strict-mode cohort of three configured voices silently runs as two and can clear the merge gate. The only signal is a logger.info line, which most runners do not surface. Strict mode's contract ('every configured provider must be available or fail') is weakened without any operator-visible warning, and the operator explicitly configured the voice.
findings.failure_mode: Operators relying on strict mode to guarantee the full cohort get a reduced review with an APPROVED verdict and no warning-level signal; a misconfigured mode: cli-only quietly removes the google reviewer from every PR.
findings.suggested_fix: In strict mode, treat a non-empty keyStatus.notPlanned as a configuration error (throw, or at minimum logger.warn naming the key). In graceful mode, log the dropped voice at warn rather than info, and consider surfacing it in the posted Verdict Quality summary so the reduced cohort is visible on the PR.

findings.description: The merge-block check previously guaranteed that zero results could never pass (0 !== models.length). The new form models.length - notPlanned.length admits the degenerate case where every configured voice is agy-routed with opt-in off (e.g. gemini-headless plus a google HTTP model under cli-only): modelResults is empty, the count check passes, .some(error) is false, and the outcome depends entirely on computeVerdictBand([]) returning something other than 'APPROVED' for an empty list. If that helper uses an every()-style all-approved check, an empty cohort reads as APPROVED and mergeBlocked stays false. No early guard for an empty keyStatus.valid is visible in the diff.
findings.failure_mode: A review with zero participating voices could leave mergeBlocked false, inverting the 'incomplete participation can never clear a merge' invariant the comment above the check states.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit guard: compute plannedCount = models.length - notPlanned.length and set mergeBlocked = true when plannedCount === 0 or modelResults.length === 0, independent of computeVerdictBand. Add a test with all voices not planned.

findings.description: The new default parameter gate: AgyGate = readAgyGate() turns a previously pure env-only function into one that spawns a synchronous yq subprocess and reads .loa.config.yaml relative to the process CWD. The pipeline passes an explicit repoRoot-based path, but any other caller that still invokes validateApiKeys(config) (startup preflight, CLI key check, dist consumers) now reads a potentially different config than the pipeline and can report a different valid/missing/notPlanned split for the same run.
findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent gating between a startup key check and the per-PR pipeline when CWD differs from repoRoot; surprising subprocess spawn from a function callers reasonably assume is pure.
findings.suggested_fix: Make gate a required parameter (or accept repoRoot and derive the path inside), and audit existing callers so every site resolves the gate from the same repoRoot path the pipeline uses.

findings.description: isAgyRouted hardcodes the literal 'gemini-headless' while the module already exposes isHeadlessModelId(modelId, provider) backed by GENERATED_MODEL_REGISTRY. If codegen adds or renames a google headless id, or an alias resolves to it, the gate misses it: the voice is planned, dispatched, refused by cheval, and the merge blocks as a failed voice rather than being recorded as not planned.
findings.failure_mode: Registry drift silently reintroduces the 'planned voice that cannot exist' case FR-1 is meant to remove, with no test catching it because the test also pins the literal.
findings.suggested_fix: Use isHeadlessModelId(modelId, 'google') (or a registry flag) in place of the string literal, and add a test that iterates the generated registry's google headless ids.

findings.cross_file_justification: The function re-derives what loa_cheval/providers/anthropic_adapter.py and the other provider adapters put on the wire, but does so from the provider NAME (`provider == "anthropic"`) plus a hardcoded assumption that every non-anthropic HTTP adapter ignores CompletionRequest.effort. Adapter dispatch elsewhere in cheval is by provider `type`, not name.
findings.description: `_effort_on_wire` is the sole source for both the MODELINV `effort_effective` field and the operator-facing dry-run line `effort: X (caller) → effective none (omitted on <model>)`. It keys on the provider key string `"anthropic"` rather than the provider's `type`, and returns None for every other HTTP provider by assertion rather than by asking the adapter. Any catalog provider of anthropic type under a different key (a Bedrock/Vertex HTTP route, a regional mirror, a test provider) will be reported as `effort_effective: null` and the dry-run will tell the operator the value is omitted while the adapter actually sends `output_config.effort`. The same misreport happens if any other adapter (OpenAI `reasoning_effort` is the obvious candidate) reads `request.effort` now or later; nothing ties this function to the adapters, so it will silently drift.
findings.failure_mode: Audit telemetry and the dry-run report state the opposite of what was sent for any provider the hardcoded branch does not recognise. Operators relying on the dry-run line to confirm an effort downgrade/omission get a false answer; the trajectory record is wrong without any error.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the provider's `type` from `hounfour["providers"][provider]` and branch on that, or better, add a small `wire_effort(model_id, effort) -> Optional[str]` classmethod/hook on each adapter (Anthropic delegates to `_effort_for_model`, headless returns passthrough, others return None) and have `_effort_on_wire` call it through `get_adapter`'s class lookup. Add a test that iterates every provider in the live catalog and asserts the derived value agrees with the adapter's actual body/argv builder.

findings.cross_file_justification: loa_cheval/providers/claude_headless_adapter.py keeps its legacy rung: when `request.effort` is None it reads `model_cfg.extra.effort` itself and passes `--effort <raw>` (confirmed by test_cli_adapter_extra_effort_stays_below_the_chokepoint_value in this diff). cheval's resolver now sits in front of that rung but does not disable it.
findings.description: For a CLI entry, `resolve_effort` validates `extra.effort` / `extra.reasoning_effort` against `_EFFORT_LEVELS` and, on an invalid value (e.g. `ultra`, or a typo), silently returns `(None, "none")` with no WARN (unlike the `default_effort` branch, which warns once). The request is dispatched with `effort=None`, and the headless adapter's legacy rung then reads the same raw `extra.effort` and passes `--effort ultra` to the CLI. MODELINV records `effort` absent, `effort_source: none`, `effort_effective` absent, and the docstring's claim for the `none` rung ("nothing on the wire, the vendor default applies") is false for exactly this case. The CLI receiving the raw value is pre-existing behaviour; the new part is that the chokepoint now asserts in the audit record that nothing was sent.
findings.failure_mode: A misconfigured CLI entry produces an audit envelope that says no effort was requested while the spawned CLI received an invalid `--effort` value (and likely fails with a CLI argument error that the envelope gives no clue about). The one-WARN-per-reason policy also has a gap: invalid `extra.effort` is the only invalid catalog value that is swallowed with no log line.
findings.suggested_fix: (1) Emit `_effort_warn_once((model_key, "invalid_extra"), ...)` when a CLI entry's `extra` value fails `_valid_effort`, mirroring the `default_effort` branch. (2) Either remove the headless adapter's legacy `extra.effort` fallback now that cheval resolves it (the adapter is only reached via cheval), or have cheval pass an explicit sentinel so the adapter does not re-read `extra` when the resolver already evaluated it. Add a test asserting that for `{kind: cli, extra: {effort: "ultra"}}` the built argv carries no `--effort`.

findings.description: The effort enum is now maintained in at least four independent places: `_EFFORT_LEVELS` in cheval.py (this diff), the argparse `--effort` choices, `params.default_effort.enum` in model-config-v3.schema.json, and `effort_effective.enum` in model-invoke-complete.payload.schema.json (both asserted by the new test). `resolve_effort` trusts the argparse-validated caller value unconditionally but validates catalog values against its own copy, so if any one list gains or loses a level the rungs disagree: a level argparse accepts could be rejected from the catalog with a misleading 'not one of' WARN, or a catalog value could be accepted that the trajectory schema then rejects. Separately, the parameter docstrings added to `emit_model_invoke_complete` and the emit-site comment in `cmd_invoke` still read `caller | catalog | none`, omitting the `extra` value the resolver actually produces and the schema test requires.
findings.failure_mode: Enum drift between the four copies produces inconsistent acceptance across caller, catalog, and audit-schema layers with no test catching it; the stale `caller | catalog | none` docstrings mislead the next consumer of the MODELINV contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the levels once (e.g. in loa_cheval/types.py next to CompletionRequest) and import it for `_EFFORT_LEVELS`, the argparse `choices`, and a test that loads both JSON schemas and asserts their enums equal the constant. Update the two docstrings/comments to `caller | catalog | extra | none`.

findings.description: The entry raises effective_input_ceiling and probed_ceiling from 180000 to 936000, justified in the comment as the I2 invariant 'input ceiling + default max_tokens <= context_window' using a 64,000 'default output budget'. The same entry (visible two lines above in the hunk) advertises max_output_tokens: 128000. 936,000 + 128,000 = 1,064,000 > context_window 1,000,000, so the invariant only holds for the implicit default, not for the output budget the catalog itself advertises as legal. The clamp also sits exactly at the hard limit with zero margin for anything the pre-dispatch gate does not count: adapter system prompt, tool definitions, cache-creation tokens, the headless CLI's own system prompt (the 972,887 measurement includes it), and estimator under-count — the implementation report documents the probe's own estimator under-counting ~1.8x on this tokenizer, yet the dispatch-time gate necessarily compares an estimate against this measured-token ceiling.
findings.failure_mode: (a) Any caller passing --max-tokens above 64000 (up to the advertised 128000) with an input between ~872K and 936K estimated tokens passes cheval's ceiling check and is rejected by Anthropic/Bedrock with a 400 (prompt tokens + max_tokens exceeds the context window; Claude 3.7+ validates this rather than truncating). (b) Any input cheval or Bridgebuilder (maxInput 916000) estimates just under the ceiling but which tokenizes a few percent higher is hard-rejected by the API or the CLI pre-flight ('~N tokens (limit 1000000)') instead of being truncated. With the previous 180K ceiling both cases were impossible (5x headroom); large dissent/Bridgebuilder inputs that previously truncated and succeeded will now fail outright.
findings.suggested_fix: Clamp with the entry's advertised output budget: effective_input_ceiling = context_window - max_output_tokens = 872,000 (or make the I2 check and i2_clamped() use max_output_tokens, not the default). Reserve an explicit safety margin below the hard limit for estimator error (e.g. divide by the observed tokenizer_ratio from the probe record, or a fixed 5-10%). At dispatch, have cheval cap max_tokens to context_window - input so a near-ceiling request degrades output length rather than failing.

findings.description: The bound was measured through claude-headless on Bedrock (cli_model global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5) but is written onto the providers.anthropic HTTP-API entry, whose beta_headers is [] in the same hunk. The reprobe_trigger itself states the API transport has not been probed. The cycle-126 beta_headers mechanism exists precisely for dated 1M-context flags; if the direct API route for this model needs one, the API route now admits up to 936K tokens into a window that rejects them, whereas 180K was safe on either route.
findings.failure_mode: Dispatches to anthropic:claude-opus-5-5 over the HTTP API with inputs between 180K and 936K are sent instead of refused/truncated and fail with a provider 400 if the API route's context window differs from the Bedrock CLI route's.
findings.suggested_fix: Run tools/ceiling-probe-live.py --transport api from a host with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY before raising the API-route entry, or keep the API-route ceiling conservative and attach the headless measurement to the claude-headless route (or a transport-scoped override) until the API bound is verified.

findings.description: The new schema description for measured_input_tokens says it is 'the value written to probed_ceiling / effective_input_ceiling'. The catalog in the same change writes measured_input_tokens: 972887 but probed_ceiling and effective_input_ceiling: 936000, and commit 8ad37c55 makes the tool deliberately keep the raw measurement in measured_input_tokens while writing the I2-clamped value to the ceilings. The schema description now contradicts both the data and the tool. probed_ceiling also carries a non-measured value under method: probed_headless.
findings.failure_mode: Readers (staleness/reprobe logic, /loa status, future migrations) that follow the schema text will assume probed_ceiling == measured_input_tokens and either mis-report calibration or 'correct' the clamp back to 972887, re-exposing the context-window overflow.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the description to 'the raw accepted input size the provider reported; probed_ceiling/effective_input_ceiling hold this value after cheval's I2 clamp (context_window - output budget) and may be lower'. Consider writing the raw measurement to probed_ceiling and only the clamp to effective_input_ceiling so the two fields carry distinct meanings.

findings.description: The tool's own outcome was `partial` and by design it writes nothing on partial; the lead invoked write_catalog_operator_set() manually. The resulting entry (source: operator_set, method: probed_headless, transport, cli_version, cli_model, measured_input_tokens, calibrated_at) is byte-for-byte the shape the tool writes on a `clean` outcome, and sample_size is null despite five recorded samples. The only indication that the bisection did not converge is a YAML comment, which every structured reader drops.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream consumers (staleness checks, /loa status 'calibrated', Bridgebuilder budget codegen, future audits) cannot distinguish a tool-verified clean probe from a manual write off a partial run; the provenance the schema was extended to carry is misleading for this entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the outcome in structured form: add an `outcome` (clean|partial) or `verified_steps` field to ceiling_calibration, set sample_size to the number of samples actually taken (5, or 3 accepts), and have write_catalog_operator_set() refuse or mark the entry when the source record's outcome is not clean.

findings.description: Both hunks labelled `.claude/adapters/cheval.py` contain JSON Schema (params.default_effort and the ceiling_calibration provenance fields), i.e. the content of .claude/data/schemas/model-config-v3.schema.json. None of the Python the report describes (resolve_effort, _effort_on_wire, the three CompletionRequest sites, the dry-run effort line, modelinv.py effort_source/effort_effective) appears in the diff, yet the new bats cases c127-2-1..3 assert on resolved_model/effort/effort_source/effort_effective in cheval's --dry-run output. Either the diff is mis-pathed or the code under test is missing from the review set.
findings.failure_mode: If the path is literal, cheval.py would not parse. More likely the diff is incomplete and the primary reviewer has approved behavioural tests against code they have not seen; the effort-resolution precedence, the 'resolved once' semantics across fallback hops, and the WARN dedupe cannot be verified.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-generate the diff so the schema hunks carry their real path and the cheval.py / modelinv.py changes are included, then re-review resolve_effort (particularly what effort_source a fallback hop reports when the primary entry supplied the catalog default and the answering entry has none).

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff's _measured() predicate is what lets the suite accept the new claude-opus-5-5 catalog entry (effective_input_ceiling 936000, ceiling_calibration.transport: claude-headless, cli_model: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5). That field on an auth_type: http_api entry is consumed by cheval._lookup_max_input_tokens / loa_cheval.routing.ceiling.input_bound to gate direct Anthropic HTTP dispatch, and the diff's test_legacy_wall_applies_only_to_anthropic_under_the_kill_switch now asserts the HTTP gate equals that CLI-measured value.
findings.description: _measured() honors any operator_set/empirical_probe calibration with calibrated_at, with no check that ceiling_calibration.transport matches the entry's dispatch path. The only measured entry it admits was probed through `claude -p` over Bedrock (transport claude-headless), yet it is the http_api entry whose ceiling moved from 180K (which the same test's docstring says was 'probed under streaming' on the HTTP route) to 936K. The HTTP route's account_limits remain tier: unverified, itpm: null, so nothing on the HTTP transport has demonstrated acceptance of a 936K-token request.
findings.failure_mode: cheval's walk gate now admits HTTP requests to claude-opus-5-5 between 180K and 936K input tokens. If the direct API account rejects them (400 prompt-too-long, 429 ITPM, or a tier gate on the 1M window), the call fails after the payload is built and falls back to anthropic:claude-opus-5 whose ceiling is still 180K, so the fallback cannot carry the same request either. The suite stays green because the test follows the catalog value rather than a transport-matched measurement.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the calibration transport-aware: in _measured (and ideally in input_bound) only treat a calibration as governing an http_api entry when cal.get('transport') is absent or 'api'; add an assertion in test_every_http_entry_has_ceiling_with_provenance that a calibrated http_api entry's transport is compatible with auth_type. Alternatively run the probe's --transport api path once for claude-opus-5-5 on the HTTP route before raising the HTTP ceiling, and record the headless measurement under the entry that actually dispatches through the CLI.

findings.description: For measured entries `cap = entry['effective_input_ceiling']`, so `expected = min(effective, cw - dmt)` and the assertion `effective == expected` reduces to the I1 check on the next line: the test is tautological for exactly the entries the cycle introduced, and the recorded measurement (ceiling_calibration.measured_input_tokens 972887) is never compared to the written 936000. test_legacy_wall_applies_only_to_anthropic_under_the_kill_switch likewise derives `want` from _measured(), a test-local reimplementation of the runtime's calibrated predicate that already diverges from input_bound in two ways: it filters on source (kf_derived + calibrated_at is 'calibrated' to the runtime per test_i1_and_i2_per_entry_from_the_fields but not to _measured), and it ignores stale_after_days. The module already has the right pattern in test_walk_gate_threshold_is_the_policy_bound_not_the_literal, which asks input_bound for the expected value.
findings.failure_mode: The I2 clamp the report says the lead applied by hand (and which the tool's clean path previously omitted) is unchecked against the measurement: a future write of probed_ceiling/effective_input_ceiling = measured_input_tokens that happens to satisfy I1 (e.g. a smaller max_tokens default) would pass. Any future divergence between _measured() and input_bound (a kf_derived calibration with a non-180K value, or staleness handling in the runtime after 2027-01-05 for the current entry) flips test_legacy_wall_applies_only_to_anthropic_under_the_kill_switch red or, worse, keeps it green while the gate serves a different number than the test believes.
findings.suggested_fix: For measured entries assert `effective_input_ceiling == min(cal['measured_input_tokens'], context_window - _default_max_tokens(entry))` and `probed_ceiling == effective_input_ceiling`; compute `want` in the legacy-wall test via `input_bound(entry, max_tokens=_default_max_tokens(entry)).value` instead of _measured(), and keep _measured() only for the shape checks in test_opus_5_5_has_the_1m_window_at_standard_pricing.

findings.description: The module-scoped guard asserts that .run/model-invoke.jsonl (cheval's MODELINV ledger) is byte-identical before and after the module, and the docstring presents this as proof that 'no live call escaped the fake'. On the claude-headless transport the probe spawns ${CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN:-claude} directly via subprocess (record['argv'] == [bin, *PINNED]); a real `claude -p` never writes cheval's ledger, so the guard cannot observe the one spend path this module exercises. test_runs_from_another_cwd_under_python_isolated_mode builds its own environment rather than using the `fake` fixture, so a future edit that drops the CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN assignment there would run the real CLI with --budget-usd 20 and still satisfy the guard.
findings.failure_mode: A test that reaches the real CLI bisects a 400K-token Opus 5.5 prompt for up to the $20 budget per test, on the operator's Bedrock/API account, and the module reports zero live spend.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the guard fail-closed for this transport: at module setup set CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN to a non-existent path (and PATH to an empty dir for the PATH test) so any test that forgets the fake fails on spawn; and/or have each test assert that fake['calls']() is non-empty and that record['cli_bin'] equals the fake path. Keep the ledger check only where the API transport is exercised.

findings.description: The test pins the budget pre-flight at 'worst-case step ≈ $1.60' for a 400K-token step and '12 such steps fit in $20', i.e. input_per_mtok ($4/MTok) only. The fake, like the real CLI, reports the prompt under usage.cache_creation_input_tokens, which the Anthropic API bills at 1.25× input, so the worst-case step is ≈$2.00 and only 10 such steps fit in $20. The record labels this pricing_basis: catalog_estimate.
findings.failure_mode: If the budget gate stops on the catalog estimate rather than the CLI's total_cost_usd, a run of all-accepted steps can spend ≈$25 against a $20 --budget-usd before the tool declares the budget exhausted; the live run happened to under-spend only because CLI-preflight rejections cost nothing while being estimated at full price.
findings.suggested_fix: Price cache_creation_input_tokens at 1.25× input in the estimate (or add cache_write_per_mtok to the catalog and read it), prefer the CLI's total_cost_usd for the running total when present, and update the pinned strings to the corrected figures.

findings.description: Pytest test code appears to have been added inside the production provider module. The added module body includes `@pytest.mark.parametrize(...)` decorators, but production imports of `loa_cheval.providers.claude_headless_adapter` will evaluate those decorators at import time.
findings.failure_mode: If `pytest` is not imported in this runtime module, importing the Claude headless adapter raises `NameError: name 'pytest' is not defined`, breaking any command path that loads the provider. Even if pytest were imported, this leaves test-only fixtures and helper references in production code.
findings.suggested_fix: Move these test functions into the intended test module, likely `.claude/adapters/tests/test_ceiling_probe_cli_transport.py`, and keep `.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/claude_headless_adapter.py` limited to runtime adapter code.

findings.description: The new usage docstring states that a clean --write-catalog writes `probed_ceiling` and `effective_input_ceiling` = "the measured accepted size (raw — the api transport applies no safety margin either)". The same diff ships fr23b tests (`test_the_write_clamps_to_the_i2_invariant_and_keeps_the_raw_measurement`, `test_clean_end_to_end_write_above_the_clamp`) asserting the written value is min(measured, context_window − default_max_tokens(entry)) = 936,000 with the raw accept only in `ceiling_calibration.measured_input_tokens`. The docstring also still describes `--tolerance-tokens` without saying it is now in measured tokens, and the older 'Exit codes' line still defines 3 as 'the budget cap stopped the bisection' while the new paragraph makes 3 mean any partial.
findings.failure_mode: An operator reading --help expects the raw measurement in the catalog and a filler-unit tolerance; the tool writes a clamped value and a measured-token tolerance. Misread provenance when auditing the catalog entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the docstring: the written bound is min(measured, context_window − default_max_tokens(entry)) (I2), the raw accept is kept in ceiling_calibration.measured_input_tokens, --tolerance-tokens / --max-tokens-probe are measured tokens, and exit 3 is any partial outcome.

findings.cross_file_justification: The committed record is in the diff and shows the spend rule from tools/ceiling-probe-live.py (`max(cli total_cost_usd, tokens × catalog price)` for every attempt) charging $4.00 and $2.36 for two rejections that reported `cli_reported_cost_usd: 0` and never produced billable usage (`size_origin: cli_local` pre-flight, and a provider 400). `test_transient_classes_retry_with_backoff_and_count_every_attempt` pins the same behaviour ('two rejected at the requested size' are paid for).
findings.description: Size rejections that never reach the model (the CLI's own pre-flight) or are refused with a 400 are not billed by Anthropic or Bedrock, yet the probe debits them at the full catalog input price of the requested filler size. In the committed run this consumed $6.36 of the $20 budget on zero-cost attempts; the tool's own spent_usd is 19.10 against a CLI-reported 12.74. That phantom spend is the proximate cause of the `partial` outcome ("budget cap stopped the bisection"), which in turn led to the manual catalog write that bypassed the tool's clean-only gate.
findings.failure_mode: The budget cap trips one or two bisection steps early on every run whose top steps are pre-flight rejected (which is the normal shape of a probe), producing `partial` records and no automatic write; operators then hand-write the catalog, which is exactly what the clean-only gate exists to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: For a size rejection with no usage block and a CLI-reported cost of 0 (cli_local pre-flight, or a provider 400/validation error), charge 0 (or a count_tokens-sized nominal). Keep max(cli_cost, estimate) only for attempts that returned usage or a non-zero CLI cost. Record `billed: false` on such samples so the spend line stays auditable.

findings.cross_file_justification: The test in the diff asserts that a token-budget 429 persisting through 3 attempts yields `failure_class: token_limit`, kind `size`, exit 0 (clean), so the behaviour flows into the catalog write path in tools/ceiling-probe-live.py (docstring hunk in diff). The docstring says 429 is 'retried up to 3 attempts with backoff' and only context-limit messages are size rejections; it does not say a persisted token-budget 429 is promoted to a size rejection.
findings.description: The retry backoff is 5s then 15s (`fake['sleeps'] == [5, 15]`), i.e. ~20s total, but tokens-per-minute windows are 60s. Bisection steps run back-to-back and each accepted step deposits hundreds of thousands of tokens into the window, so the *next* larger step can 429 for three straight attempts purely because of the previous step's tokens, not because the request exceeds any per-request limit. The probe then records that step as a `size` rejection above the largest accept — a shape the `_outcome_reasons` 'inconsistent' check cannot catch — and keeps bisecting below it. On a direct-Anthropic claude-headless route (API key or subscription) this converges to a 'clean' bound that is really (ITPM − previous step) and writes it to `probed_ceiling`/`effective_input_ceiling` with `method: probed_headless`. The API transport keeps rate-limit evidence in `account_limits.itpm`; the CLI transport folds it into the ceiling instead.
findings.failure_mode: A clean-looking write of an under-sized ceiling (potentially tens of percent low) into the production catalog, silently governing truncation for every cheval caller until a re-probe. Not reproducible on the Bedrock route used in Task 1.5 (Bedrock throttles as `other`), so the live run did not exercise it.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) for a token-budget 429, wait out the window (≥60s, or the retry-after header) before the final attempt and only then classify as size; or (b) classify a persisted token-budget 429 as its own class (`rate_limit`) that makes the outcome `partial` with a reason, and record the parsed per-minute limit into `account_limits.itpm` as the API path does, rather than into the ceiling.

findings.description: This test skips whenever the live catalog no longer carries the '# loa:shortcut: Opus 5's measured bound, not probed on 5.5' comment. The lead's write in f43949d6 removed that comment, so from this commit onward the test is permanently skipped on the real tree. It is the only place in the suite that (1) validates the written `ceiling_calibration` block against `$defs.ceilingCalibration` in model-config-v3.schema.json, (2) checks that every other provider/model entry and the aliases block are byte-for-byte untouched by `write_catalog_operator_set`, and (3) checks the comment-count/provenance-line invariants. The SYNTH-based tests do none of these. The implementation report states the adapters pytest selection has only one pre-existing skip outside the sprint's files; this new skip is inside them.
findings.failure_mode: A future change to `write_catalog_operator_set` that emits a schema-invalid `ceiling_calibration` field, or that disturbs a neighbouring entry's YAML, passes the suite; the drift is only caught later when the live catalog is schema-checked (if at all).
findings.suggested_fix: Move the jsonschema validation, the neighbouring-entry equality loop and the aliases check into the SYNTH-based tests (`test_a_measured_bound_below_the_old_one_is_written_as_measured` or a new SYNTH test), and either delete the live-catalog test or convert it to assert the already-calibrated catalog is idempotent under a re-write.

findings.description: The guard's docstring says it covers 'the suites whose Opus 5.5 ceiling pins were swept to read the catalog', but SWEPT lists only `test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py` and `loa-status-providers.bats`. The implementation report (Task 1.4) says LSP-5 *and the codegen tests* (gen-bb-registry-codegen.bats, gen-adapter-maps.bats, the truncation.generated.ts expectations) were swept too. Those suites are unguarded, so a literal 180000 / 180_000 (or the new 936000 / 916000) can be re-pinned there without this test noticing.
findings.failure_mode: The next re-probe that changes the Opus 5.5 bound turns the codegen suites red on a literal, which is exactly the failure mode FR-3.4 / SDD D-3.4 says this guard prevents.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the swept codegen suites to SWEPT (with an empty allow-set), and consider extending LITERAL to the current written value (936000) so a re-pin of the *calibrated* number is caught as well as a re-pin of the old cap.

findings.description: The test passes `--allow-partial` together with `--write-catalog` on the claude-headless transport and asserts the catalog is untouched and exit is 3 — i.e. the flag is accepted by argparse but has no effect on this transport, and nothing in the asserted record (`reasons`) names the ignored flag. An operator who passes `--allow-partial --write-catalog` expects a write; they get exit 3 and no change, and have to discover why.
findings.failure_mode: Silent no-op of an explicit operator flag on one transport. In Task 1.5 the lead ended up hand-calling `write_catalog_operator_set` to get the write the flag appeared to offer.
findings.suggested_fix: In `_main_cli`, either reject `--allow-partial` with `--write-catalog` as a usage error (exit 2) for the claude-headless transport, or append an explicit reason such as '--allow-partial is not honoured by the claude-headless transport; catalog not written' to `record['reasons']` and print it to stderr.

findings.description: The diff labels two large hunks (~400 lines of pytest tests referencing `tool`, `fake`, `CATALOG`, `SYNTH`, `SCHEMA_V3`, `pytest`, `yaml`) as modifications to the production adapter module, with a `-0,0` old range that cannot belong to an existing non-empty file. This is almost certainly a diff-chunking artefact: the content is `test_ceiling_probe_cli_transport.py`. Two consequences for this review: (1) if the attribution were literal, the adapter would import pytest at module load and fail in any runtime without it; (2) the adapter's *actual* production change in this sprint — the `build_headless_argv` extraction shared by the adapter and the probe — is not present in the diff and therefore has not been reviewed here.
findings.failure_mode: Unreviewed production change to the argv builder that both cheval's headless route and the probe depend on; a regression there (e.g. a dropped `--no-session-persistence` or `--tools ""`) would affect every headless completion, not just the probe.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm `git show 8ad37c55 -- .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/claude_headless_adapter.py` contains only the `build_headless_argv` extraction and no test code, and route that hunk through review.

findings.description: `_ADAPTERS_DIR` is derived from `__file__` using two `dirname()` calls and then appending `.claude/adapters`. In this diff-touched file, `__file__` is already under `.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers`, so the computed path becomes `.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/.claude/adapters`, not the real adapters root. Any `--transport claude-headless` path that calls `_adapters()` will insert the wrong directory into `sys.path` and then fail to import `loa_cheval`.
findings.failure_mode: Running the new claude-headless probe transport fails before probing with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'loa_cheval'`, so FR-3’s CLI transport is unusable from this file location.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the adapters root as the directory above `loa_cheval`, e.g. from this file use `os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))`, or otherwise reuse an existing repo-root/adapters-root resolver instead of appending `.claude/adapters` below `loa_cheval`.

findings.description: A token-budget 429 (ceiling.is_token_limit_message) is returned as kind=transient with token_limit=True; in step() when it persists over the 3 attempts (backoffs total 20s) the sample is rewritten to kind=size, failure_class=token_limit, size_origin=provider. The bisection then treats a per-minute input-token throttle as a context rejection: it becomes smallest_fail, brackets the previous accept, and _outcome_reasons reports `clean`. With --write-catalog the entry is written as method: probed_headless from a rate-limit artifact. The written value is still an accepted, needle-verified size (so the bound is conservative, never too high), but it is labeled clean and will under-report the route's real ceiling by whatever the org's ITPM happened to allow in that minute.
findings.failure_mode: An org below the top rate tier probing a 1M-window model: a large step is accepted (consuming the minute's budget), the next step hits the token 429 three times inside ~20s, is recorded as a size rejection, the bracket closes within tolerance, outcome=clean, and the catalog gets an ITPM-bounded effective_input_ceiling with no partial flag.
findings.suggested_fix: Never let a failure_class=token_limit sample satisfy the bracket: in _outcome_reasons add a reason when the smallest_fail sample's failure_class != context_limit (or exclude token_limit samples from current_fail and keep them as `other`-class stops). Alternatively lengthen the token_limit backoff to cover a full 60s window before giving up.

findings.description: step() charges `est = (measured or est_measured) * price_in // 1_000_000` for every attempt, including size rejections with size_origin=cli_local (the CLI's own pre-flight, no provider call, no billing) and OSError before spawn. The live run shows the effect: estimate $19.10 vs CLI-reported $12.74, and the $20 cap stopped the bisection (`outcome: partial`) while real spend had ~$7 of headroom. The two CLI pre-flight rejections (filler 1,000,000 and 590,000 at $4/MTok) alone account for ~$6.36 of phantom spend.
findings.failure_mode: The budget pre-check (`spent_micro + est_measured * price_in // 1_000_000 > budget_micro`) trips early, producing partial outcomes and no catalog write on runs that were in fact well within budget; operators then hand-write the catalog, which is exactly what happened in Task 1.5.
findings.suggested_fix: In step(), when res['kind']=='size' and res.get('size_origin')=='cli_local' (and for the OSError branch) charge 0 (or only rep_micro if the CLI reported a cost). Keep the full estimate for timeouts and provider-side errors, where the input may have been billed.

findings.description: `diag` is truncated to 300 characters before any classification: `is_context_limit_message(diag)`, `is_token_limit_message(diag)`, `_PROVIDER_ORIGIN.search(diag)`, `parse_context_limit(diag)` and the _TRANSIENT_MARKERS scan all run on the clipped string. The diag is assembled as result + api_status + stderr, so when the CLI emits a preamble (warnings, a JSON-wrapped API error envelope, Bedrock's `ValidationException: The model returned the following errors: ...` prefix) the limit statement or its token count can fall past the cut.
findings.failure_mode: A genuine context-limit rejection is classified as `other` (bisection stops, outcome partial, exit 1) or its `rejected_input_tokens` is lost (size_basis degrades to `scaled` and the ratio is not corrected), after the step's tokens were already paid for.
findings.suggested_fix: Classify on the untruncated diag and apply the `[:300]` only to the `detail` stored in the returned dict.

findings.description: step() guards `_run_capped` + `_classify` only against subprocess.TimeoutExpired and OSError. Any other exception from the classification path (e.g. `ceiling.parse_context_limit(diag)` returning None → AttributeError on `.get`, a non-int value flowing into `_size`/`max`, a JSON type surprise in `usage`) propagates out of _main_cli with a traceback. The record — the only artifact of the money already spent, and what the SDD says is 'always written' — is built and written only after the loop, so it is lost.
findings.failure_mode: A probe that has consumed several multi-dollar steps dies on an unanticipated classifier exception; no record file, no samples, no spent_usd, and the operator cannot tell what was learned or billed.
findings.suggested_fix: In step(), catch `Exception` around `_classify` (and `_run_capped`) and convert to `{'kind': 'other', 'detail': f'classifier error: {e!r}'}`; additionally write the record in a `try/finally` so a crash after the first attempt still persists what was measured.

findings.description: Catalog-write prerequisites are checked only after the bisection has spent its budget: i2_clamped raises when the entry has no positive context_window, and write_catalog_operator_set raises when `effective_input_ceiling:`, `probed_ceiling:` or `ceiling_calibration:` is absent at indent 8 — the normal state of a never-calibrated entry, i.e. the main use case for a probe. The failure surfaces as `catalog not written` / exit 1 after a clean (paid) run. Separately, `--allow-partial`, `--tier` and `--itpm` are accepted by argparse but silently ignored when `--transport claude-headless`; an operator passing `--allow-partial --write-catalog` (the Task 1.5 situation) gets no write and no warning.
findings.failure_mode: A $20 clean probe of a fresh model entry ends with 'catalog not written: … `ceiling_calibration` not found in the entry'; or an operator relies on --allow-partial and discovers after the run that it had no effect on this transport.
findings.suggested_fix: At the top of _main_cli, when --write-catalog is set, read the catalog and run i2_clamped plus a dry write_catalog_operator_set with a placeholder ceiling (discarding the result) to fail fast before any spend. Either honor --allow-partial on the headless path or make argparse reject --allow-partial/--tier/--itpm with --transport claude-headless.

findings.description: `subprocess.run(..., timeout=timeout)` kills only the direct child on TimeoutExpired. The documented route runs through a wrapper (`claude-bedrock`, CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN); unless that wrapper `exec`s the CLI, SIGKILL on the wrapper leaves the real `claude` node process alive to finish the ~1M-token request. step() then classifies the timeout as transient, sleeps 5s, and sends the same prompt again.
findings.failure_mode: On a slow step two or three concurrent 1M-token requests run against the same account: billed input the budget accounting never sees, plus self-inflicted 429s that the next attempt may record as a token_limit → size rejection (see DISS-001).
findings.suggested_fix: Launch with `start_new_session=True` and on TimeoutExpired send `os.killpg(proc.pid, SIGKILL)` (use Popen + communicate(timeout=) rather than subprocess.run), then re-raise; also rmtree the workspace after the group is dead.

findings.description: For a ProviderUnavailableError the transient decision includes `_STATUS_5XX.search(diag)` with pattern `\b5\d\d\b` over the free-text diag. Any word-delimited 3-digit number starting with 5 matches: node stack-trace positions (`cli.js:512:13`), line counts, ids. A deterministic CLI crash on a large prompt (OOM, a thrown error with a stack) whose stderr contains such a number is retried as transient.
findings.failure_mode: Two extra full-size attempts (each charged at est, ~$4 per 1M-token step at the catalog price) plus 20s of backoff for an error that cannot succeed, draining the budget cap and pushing the run to partial.
findings.suggested_fix: Anchor the 5xx match to a status context, e.g. `(?:status|http|error)[ :=]+5\d\d\b` or `\b5\d\d\b(?=\s*(?:internal|service|bad gateway|overloaded))`, mirroring how _PROVIDER_ORIGIN already requires explicit markers.

findings.cross_file_justification: The new ceiling bullet documents a catalog write (.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml claude-opus-5-5.ceiling_calibration.calibrated_at) that, per the cycle-126 I2 contract stated in the same hunk, switches loa_cheval/routing/ceiling.py from the probed/preempt path to trusting the calibrated bound for the HTTP adapter.
findings.description: The Opus 5.5 ceiling bullet records `calibrated_at` on the `claude-opus-5-5` entry from a measurement taken through the headless CLI on Bedrock (`method: probed_headless`, `transport: claude-headless`). The cycle-126 bullet in the same [Unreleased] section defines `calibrated_at` as the signal that the HTTP adapter's I2 gate trusts the calibrated bound instead of the probed 180,000 with preempt/warn. The direct-API transport was never probed (the bullet's own `reprobe_trigger` names the API-transport probe as outstanding) and `account_limits` remains `{tier: unverified, itpm: null}`. The CHANGELOG does not say that the HTTP route now trusts a bound measured on a different transport and host.
findings.failure_mode: An `opus` HTTP request between 180K and 936K input tokens that previously preempted locally with the calibration command now goes to the wire. If the direct API or the account's tier rejects it, the call fails as PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT after one retry and is not walked; because the entry is calibrated, the `.run/ceiling-observed.json` observation does not lower the bound, so the failure recurs on every such request. Requests that are accepted above 200K are billed at the long-context multiplier the cycle-126 bullet documents as `verified: false`.
findings.suggested_fix: Scope the calibration to the transport that measured it: have the I2 policy treat `ceiling_calibration.transport != http` as uncalibrated for the HTTP adapter (keep preempt/warn there until `ceiling-probe-live.py --model claude-opus-5-5` runs over the API), or record the 936,000 bound on the CLI hop's entry only. If the operator decision stands, state in the bullet that the HTTP gate now trusts a CLI/Bedrock-measured bound and that `account_limits` is unverified.

findings.description: The probe bullet states that only a `clean` outcome writes the catalog and that the write sets `probed_ceiling`/`effective_input_ceiling` "to the measured bound". The ceiling bullet then presents the catalog write as a probe result. The implementation report discloses that the live run's outcome was `partial` (the $20 cap stopped the bisection before the 16K tolerance), that the tool wrote nothing, that the lead wrote the entry by hand through `write_catalog_operator_set()`, and that commit 8ad37c55 changed the clean write path to apply the I2 clamp (raw measurement kept in `measured_input_tokens`). None of this is in the CHANGELOG. In the same [Unreleased] section the cycle-126 bullet still describes `probed_ceiling` as "(180,000, the last measured bound)", which the new bullet contradicts.
findings.failure_mode: A reader of the release notes concludes the 936,000 bound came from a clean tool run and that the tool writes the raw measured value, neither of which is true. An operator reproducing the calibration with `--write-catalog` expects a write on the same evidence and gets none (partial outcome), and an operator reading the clean-path contract expects `probed_ceiling == measured_input_tokens`.
findings.suggested_fix: In the ceiling bullet, state the tool outcome (`partial`) and that the entry was written by the operator via `write_catalog_operator_set()` with the I2 clamp applied. In the probe bullet, say the clean write sets the ceiling to the I2-clamped measured bound and keeps the raw value in `measured_input_tokens`. Amend the cycle-126 parenthetical to something like "(the last measured bound; 180,000 before cycle-127)".

findings.cross_file_justification: The effort bullet documents cheval.resolve_effort's precedence (caller > catalog default of the resolved entry > CLI entry's extra.effort > none) and the catalog change (.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml: only claude-opus-5-5 sets params.default_effort). The claude-headless entry, which the cycle-126 bullet names as the opus alias's chain fallback and the dissent companion/repair hop, is not given a default.
findings.description: The bullet is titled "Claude Opus 5.5 reasons at `high` by default" and says the resolution applies "for both the HTTP adapter and the headless CLI". The default is a per-entry catalog value and the report says only `claude-opus-5-5` sets it. The `claude-headless` entry carries none, so when a request walks from `opus` to `claude-headless`, or when the dissent companion/repair chain starts at `claude-headless`, the hop passes `--effort` only if a legacy `extra.effort` is set. The probe record shows this host's CLI runs `global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5`, so that route runs at the vendor default `medium`, the exact regression FR-2 set out to close.
findings.failure_mode: On a fallback or CLI-first route (OpenAI-family primary's companion `opus → claude-headless`, the repair chain's `claude-headless` hop, or any `opus` call whose HTTP hop fails over), Opus 5.5 reasons at `medium` while the MODELINV envelope records `effort_source: none` and the CHANGELOG promises `high`. Verdict quality on the dissent's Claude voice is silently one reasoning level below what the release notes state.
findings.suggested_fix: Either set `params.default_effort: high` on the CLI entries whose configured model is Opus 5.5 (`claude-headless` at least), or carry the effort resolved for the originally requested entry across the chain walk when the hop's own entry declares no default, and add a test that the `opus → claude-headless` fallback argv contains `--effort high`. If neither is done, qualify the CHANGELOG claim to the HTTP entry.

findings.cross_file_justification: The new 'Cycle-127 addendum' bullet documents the agy refusal as `INVALID_CONFIG`, and the implementation report confirms `AgyOptInRequiredError` maps to `INVALID_CONFIG`. grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-1.6 (context line in this same diff, unchanged) specifies the refusal as `ROUTE_DISABLED` / `failure_class: opt_in_required`. The same commit ships a normative design record and user-facing migration doc that disagree on the error code.
findings.description: SDD D-1.6 names the opt-in refusal `ROUTE_DISABLED`; the migration addendum, the e2e refusal transcript and the adapter emit `INVALID_CONFIG`. The implementer's report lists a deviation from D-1.5 but not from D-1.6, so this drift is undocumented. The migration doc also asserts the refusal is 'never a breaker trip'; that guarantee was specified for a distinct ROUTE_DISABLED class, and reusing the generic INVALID_CONFIG class means it is inherited from whatever the breaker already does for config errors rather than being a property of this gate.
findings.failure_mode: Any consumer (bash planner, Bridgebuilder, downstream mount) written against the SDD matches on `ROUTE_DISABLED` and never recognises the refusal, treating the voice as a generic failure instead of 'not planned'; conversely if the breaker counts INVALID_CONFIG as a failure, repeated refusals on a host with the opt-in off trip the google headless breaker, contradicting the migration doc.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one: either update D-1.6 to `INVALID_CONFIG` / `failure_class: opt_in_required` and add a test asserting the breaker ignores that (code, failure_class) pair, or introduce the `ROUTE_DISABLED` code in `types.py` and `AgyOptInRequiredError` and update the migration bullet and e2e transcript. Record the choice as an explicit deviation in the report.

findings.cross_file_justification: The addendum states 'cheval now preempts above 936,000 instead of 180,000 for `opus`' and 'Downstream mounts inherit the value with the catalog'. `effective_input_ceiling` in `.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml` is a per-model field read by cheval's preemption regardless of transport, but the measurement was taken only through `claude-bedrock` via the headless CLI (`ceiling_calibration.transport: claude-headless`, `cli_model: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5`).
findings.description: A transport- and route-specific measurement (Bedrock global inference profile, CLI 2.1.292 pre-flight at 1,000,000) has been written into a transport-agnostic catalog field. The HTTP adapter path for `claude-opus-5-5` and every downstream mount now lose the 180,000 preemption floor without any measurement of their route. The `reprobe_trigger` naming the API-transport probe acknowledges the gap but nothing enforces it.
findings.failure_mode: On a route whose effective window for this model is smaller (direct API tier without the 1M window, a different Bedrock region/profile, an older CLI pre-flight), prompts between 180K and 936K are no longer preempted and are uploaded in full before the provider rejects them, adding latency and, where the provider bills on rejected oversize requests, spend; Bridgebuilder's generated `maxInput 916000` truncation budget inherits the same assumption.
findings.suggested_fix: Either scope the calibrated ceiling to the recorded transport (cheval applies `probed_ceiling` only when the dispatch transport matches `ceiling_calibration.transport`, falling back to the prior floor otherwise), or state in the migration addendum and the catalog comment that HTTP-route callers and downstream mounts must re-probe before relying on the new bound, and keep the 180K floor as an explicit `fallback_ceiling` field until the API-transport probe runs.

findings.description: §1.6 records that the tool's outcome was `partial` and it 'wrote nothing', after which the lead invoked `write_catalog_operator_set()` by hand and then edited the value to 936,000. The migration addendum in the same diff tells operators the tool 'writes the catalog only on a clean outcome'. The provenance that this entry came from a partial run plus a manual clamp lives only in a YAML comment on the catalog entry; the structured `ceiling_calibration` block carries `method: probed_headless` with no outcome field, and `probed_ceiling` holds the clamped 936,000 rather than anything the probe observed.
findings.failure_mode: The catalog is round-tripped by `tools/regen-model-artifacts.sh`, yq overlays and the probe's own writer; a comment-only provenance note is dropped on the first structured rewrite, after which the entry is indistinguishable from a clean tool-produced calibration. A later operator re-running the probe, or the `test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py` `_measured` branch, has no way to tell that the bisection never closed to tolerance.
findings.suggested_fix: Add structured fields to `ceiling_calibration` (`probe_outcome: partial`, `written_by: operator`, `clamp: i2`) and extend the schema additively; have `write_catalog_operator_set()` refuse or require an explicit `--force-partial` flag when the record's outcome is not `clean`, so the bypass is visible in argv and the record. Reword the migration bullet so 'writes only on a clean outcome' and 'written from a partial run' are not presented as the same path.

findings.cross_file_justification: The addendum claims 'cheval now preempts above 936,000'. That number is in server-measured tokens (`usage` from the CLI's JSON). The same diff (sdd.md §1.6) reports the probe's own filler estimate under-counted by ≈1.8x against measured usage. Whether cheval's preemption estimator in `cheval.py` counts in the same unit is not stated anywhere in the diff, and the 8ad37c55 fix to step the bisection in measured tokens shows the unit mismatch was real inside this very tool.
findings.description: The catalog bound is expressed in measured tokens, but cheval's preemption necessarily uses a local estimate before dispatch. The run demonstrated that a heuristic estimate for this tokenizer can be off by 1.8x. If cheval's estimator shares that bias, '936,000 estimated' corresponds to roughly 1.68M real tokens and the preemption never fires before the CLI pre-flight rejects; if it is calibrated to measured tokens the doc should say so. Additionally the CLI's `usage` includes the CLI's own system prompt and tool definitions, which cheval's prompt-side count may not include, so I2 (`936,000 + 64,000 = 1,000,000`) sits exactly at the window with no margin for that overhead.
findings.failure_mode: Prompts that cheval believes are under the ceiling are rejected after upload by the CLI pre-flight or the provider with 'Prompt is too long', reproducing the failure mode the preemption exists to prevent, at the largest and most expensive request sizes.
findings.suggested_fix: State in the addendum which estimator cheval's preemption uses and that it is calibrated to measured tokens (or apply the observed `tokenizer_ratio` from the probe record when comparing). Reserve a documented margin for the CLI's fixed overhead in the I2 clamp (for example write `effective_input_ceiling = context_window - default_max_tokens - cli_overhead_tokens`) and have the probe record the overhead by measuring an empty-prompt call.
